## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the deployment, retrieval, and documentation
of passive (diffusion-based) air samplers for time-integrated
measurement of gaseous air pollutants. Passive samplers require no
pump or power supply: the target gas diffuses along a concentration
gradient through a defined path length and is captured by a sorbent or
reactive medium at the closed end of the tube. After a known exposure
period, the sampler is sealed, returned to the laboratory, and
analyzed to determine the time-weighted average ambient concentration
[@palmes1976; @cape2009].

Common target analytes include nitrogen dioxide (NO~2~), ozone (O~3~),
sulfur dioxide (SO~2~), ammonia (NH~3~), and volatile organic compounds
(VOCs). Passive samplers are widely used in spatial surveys and
community-based exposure studies because they are inexpensive,
silent, and require no electricity, making dense network deployments
feasible [@vardoulakis2009].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Deployment and retrieval of passive diffusion tube
  samplers (e.g., Palmes tubes for NO~2~, Ogawa badges for NO~2~/O~3~,
  Radiello cartridges for VOCs/NH~3~) at EA Program field sites
- **Does not apply to:** Active (pump-based) gas sampling; passive PM
  samplers; low-cost electronic gas sensors; laboratory analysis of
  exposed samplers (handled by the analytical laboratory or per
  analyte-specific lab SOPs)
- **Location:** EA Program field deployment sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling design, select sampler type and analytical lab |
| Trained Personnel | Deploy, retrieve, and document samplers     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent deployment |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Some sorbent media (e.g., triethanolamine for NO~2~)
  are mild irritants. Handle prepared tubes with gloves and avoid
  skin contact with the open end.
- **Traffic:** Many monitoring locations are near roadways. Wear a
  high-visibility vest and follow
  [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) traffic safety procedures.
- **Height:** Mounting samplers on poles or structures may require
  ladder work. Follow standard ladder safety.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling samplers)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes
- [ ] High-visibility vest (if near roadways)
- [ ] Sun protection


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Passive samplers (type matched to target analyte; see Section 6.1) | Pre-prepared by analytical lab or in-house |
| Protective rain shelters (inverted cup or tube shelter) | Shields the open end from rain and direct sunlight while allowing airflow |
| Mounting clips, zip ties, or cable ties | For attaching shelters and tubes to poles, posts, or structures |
| Airtight storage containers or bags   | For transporting unexposed and exposed samplers |
| Cooler with ice packs (for heat-sensitive sorbents) | Maintain samplers at 4 C during transport if required by the analytical lab |
| GPS unit                              | Per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Field notebook and deployment log     | For recording dates, times, and site conditions |
| Permanent marker (Sharpie)            | For labeling tubes             |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sampler Selection

Select the sampler type based on the target analyte and exposure
period:

| Target Analyte | Sampler Type           | Typical Exposure | Analytical Method |
|:---------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------|:------------------|
| NO~2~          | Palmes diffusion tube (TEA-coated grids) | 1--4 weeks | Spectrophotometry (Griess reaction) |
| NO~2~ / O~3~   | Ogawa passive sampler  | 1--2 weeks       | Spectrophotometry |
| NH~3~          | Radiello cartridge or acid-coated filter | 1--4 weeks | Spectrophotometry or IC |
| VOCs (BTEX)    | Radiello cartridge (Carbograph sorbent) or 3M OVM badge | 1--4 weeks | GC-MS (thermal desorption) |
| SO~2~          | Impregnated filter or Radiello cartridge | 1--4 weeks | Ion chromatography |

::: {.callout-note}
The analytical laboratory typically prepares and supplies the
samplers, pre-loaded with the appropriate sorbent. Confirm sampler
type, handling instructions, and shipping requirements with the lab
before each deployment.
:::

### 6.2 Pre-Deployment

1. Keep sealed samplers refrigerated (4 C) until deployment day unless
   the analytical lab specifies otherwise
2. Assign a unique ID to each sampler and record it in the deployment
   log
3. Designate at least 2 field blanks per batch: samplers that travel
   to the site, are briefly unsealed (less than 30 seconds), re-sealed,
   and returned to the lab with the exposed samplers

### 6.3 Deployment

1. At the monitoring location, mount the rain shelter at a height of
   2--3 m above ground, away from walls (at least 1 m), exhaust vents,
   and vegetation canopy
2. Remove the sampler from its sealed container, note the date and
   time, and attach the open end downward inside the rain shelter
3. Secure the sampler with clips or zip ties
4. Record in the field notebook: site ID, sampler ID, deployment
   date/time, GPS coordinates, mounting height, distance to nearest
   road, weather conditions, and any potential sources nearby
5. Photograph the installed sampler for documentation

### 6.4 Exposure Period

- The exposure period depends on the expected ambient concentration
  and the sampler's capacity. Follow the analytical lab's
  recommendation (typically 1--4 weeks for NO~2~ Palmes tubes).
- Note any unusual events during the exposure period (wildfires,
  construction, power outages affecting nearby sources) in the field
  notebook.

### 6.5 Retrieval

1. Record the retrieval date and time in the field notebook
2. Remove the sampler from the shelter, immediately cap or seal it,
   and place in an airtight container or bag
3. Calculate the total exposure time in hours
4. Place sealed samplers in a cooler with ice packs for transport (if
   required by the analytical lab)
5. Retrieve and seal the field blanks in the same manner

### 6.6 Shipping to Analytical Laboratory

1. Pack sealed samplers securely with cushioning material in an
   insulated shipping container with ice packs (if heat-sensitive)
2. Include a chain of custody form listing all sampler IDs, site
   locations, deployment and retrieval dates/times, and total exposure
   hours
3. Ship via overnight courier or deliver in person to the analytical
   lab

### 6.7 Concentration Calculation

The analytical laboratory reports the mass of analyte captured on each
sampler. The time-weighted average ambient concentration is calculated
using Fick's first law of diffusion:

$$
C = \frac{m}{D \times A / L \times t}
$$

where:

- $C$ = ambient concentration (ug/m^3^ or ppb, after unit conversion)
- $m$ = mass of analyte on the sampler (ug)
- $D$ = molecular diffusion coefficient of the analyte in air
  (cm^2^/s)
- $A$ = cross-sectional area of the diffusion path (cm^2^)
- $L$ = length of the diffusion path (cm)
- $t$ = exposure time (s)

::: {.callout-note}
The analytical lab typically performs this calculation using published
uptake rates for the specific sampler-analyte combination. Confirm
which party is responsible for the calculation.
:::


## 7. Quality Control

- Deploy at least 2 field blanks per batch (minimum 10% of total
  samplers). Field blank analyte mass should be below the method
  detection limit; if not, subtract the mean field blank mass from
  all samples.
- Deploy co-located duplicate samplers at 10% of sites. Duplicates
  should agree within 20% for NO~2~ Palmes tubes [@cape2009].
- If collocating with an active reference sampler (chemiluminescence
  NO~2~ analyzer, UV O~3~ analyzer), compare the passive sampler
  result with the reference average over the same period.
- Document any site disturbances (construction, shelter damage,
  vandalism) that could affect results.
- Archive field notebooks and chain of custody forms with the project
  data.


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Exposed Palmes tubes (TEA grids) | Return to analytical lab or dispose as chemical waste (TEA is a mild irritant) |
| Radiello cartridges (used)    | Return to analytical lab                 |
| Rain shelters and mounting hardware | Clean and reuse                    |

## 11. Training Record

Before deploying passive air samplers independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) in full
2. Review the handling instructions provided by the analytical
   laboratory for the specific sampler type
3. Observe a trained operator demonstrate deployment and retrieval at
   one site
4. Deploy and retrieve samplers at one site under supervision,
   including field blank handling
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
